Blocks.Text: The Organization Targeted Contents API returns targeted content variations configured by organization admins. These pages (also known as Life Pages or Career Pages) allow organizations to create customized views of their page for specific audiences. Admins can create multiple Life Page variations and target them to audiences based on criteria such as industry, job function, seniority, and location.
Targeted Contents (Life Pages/Career Pages) are customizable sections of a company's LinkedIn page that showcase:

Featured media (images and videos)
Featured leaders and recruiters
Employee testimonials and perspectives
Organization photos and culture
Custom content sections tailored to specific audiences

Each targeted content variation has a unique identifier and can be configured to be visible only to visitors matching specific targeting criteria, or visible to all with an option to select different variations.
This feature has been known by multiple names across LinkedIn:

Life Page - The current product name visible to users.
Targeted Content - The API and internal technical name.
Career Page - An earlier name for this feature.
All three terms refer to the same functionality: customizable organization page content that can be targeted to specific audiences.
The service currently provides the following methods:

Get - Get targeted content for a given organization targeted content key.
BatchGet - Batch get organization targeted content for the given organizations.
To successfully query the Organization Targeted Contents API, you need to obtain the proper query parameters. This section explains the prerequisites and how to construct requests.
To query this API, the authenticated user must have appropriate admin permissions for the organization. Specifically, they must have one of the following roles:

ADMINISTRATOR
CONTENT_ADMINISTRATOR
For more information on company page roles, refer to Organization Access Control.
Follow these steps to obtain the required query parameters for the Organization Targeted Contents API:

Blocks.Text: This returns a list of organization URNs that the authenticated member can query for targeted content.
Once you have an organization URN, you have two options:

Construct the organizationTargetedContentUrn directly using this format:
 Copy urn:li:organizationTargetedContent:(urn:li:organization:{ORG_ID},{TARGETED_CONTENT_ID})


Use the Organization Content Revisions API to retrieve all content revisions for an organization. This includes the targeted content configurations and their IDs.
Use the organizationTargetedContentUrn in your API request, ensure it is URL-encoded.
Example:
urn:li:organizationTargetedContent:(urn:li:organization:1234,c7e20154-c8df-12ca-aaaa-123456bbddda)
becomes:
urn%3Ali%3AorganizationTargetedContent%3A%28urn%3Ali%3Aorganization%3A1234%2Cc7e20154-c8df-12ca-aaaa-123456bbddda%29

Blocks.Text:
Attributes used to target content to users. If no attributes are specified, it means all users are targeted. Targets are
matched by OR-ing within each attribute, and AND-ing across fields. So if targeting 5 functions and 2 geo locations, the
member needs to match at least 1 function and at least 1 geo location for the target to successfully match.

Rows.Text: Top level groupings of supertitles to be targeted.
Deprecated, use geoLocations instead. Locations to be targeted.
Locations to be targeted. Each URN identifies a Bing Geo entity
Standardized degrees to be targeted. This captures members that have completed these degrees according to their education info. degrees = [BS, MS] means people who have either BS or MS degree.

Standardized fields of study to be targeted. This captures members that have studied these fields according to their education info. fieldsOfStudy = [CS, MS] means people who have either CS or MS field of study.

Standardized organizations (companies, schools, etc) to be targeted. This captures members that have added any of these organizations (schools, companies, etc) to their experience or education info. organizations = [LinkedIn (urn:li:organization:23), Microsoft (urn:li:organization:56), Stanford (urn:li:organization:33), UCLA (urn:li:organization:88)] means people who have worked at LinkedIn or Microsoft or are from Stanford or UCLA.

Blocks.Text: Note
Ensure that {ORGANIZATION_TARGETED_CONTENT_URN} needs to be URL-encoded.
An organizationTargetedContentUrn is a composite URN constructed using a targeted content ID and an organizationUrn.

GET https://api.linkedin.com/rest/dmaOrganizationTargetedContents/{ORGANIZATION_TARGETED_CONTENT_URN}

--header 'Authorization: Bearer {INSERT_TOKEN}' \
--header 'Linkedin-Version: {version number in the format YYYYMM}' \
--header 'X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0'
